To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the effect of country-of-assembly on product quality perception is moderated by country-of-design, 2) the effect of the country-of-assembly (and country-of-parts) on product quality is moderated by country of parts-source, and 3) the effect of design quality on overall quality perception is moderated when country-of-assembly is indicated as being in Mexico.

1) country-of-assembly has a positive impact on product quality perceptions, but not on design quality perceptions; 2) country-of-parts has a positive impact only on product quality perceptions; 3) country-of-design has a positive impact solely on design quality perceptions.
the country-of-origin of product components and the country in which the product is manufactured influence the perceived quality of the product.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the multidimensional construct of the country concept, and how it affects product and design quality perceptions.
understanding the impact of different dimensions of country-of-origin on consumer perceptions of product quality and design quality.
how country of origin (COO) dimensions affect consumer evaluations of product quality and design quality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

country-of-assembly has a significant impact on product quality perception, country-of-design has a significant impact in design quality perception, and country-of-parts has a significant impact only when the product is assembled in Mexico.
country-of-design and country-of-assembly are the most important country-of-origin dimensions in the context of product evaluation, followed by country-of-parts.

the country-of-design and the country-of-assembly are important determinants of product quality and design quality perceptions, and the country-of-parts is an important determinant of the design quality perception.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
consumers’ perceptions of the quality of products and designs are influenced by the country-of-assembly (COA), country-of-design (COD), and parts-source country (PSC) of a hybrid product.
consumers’ evaluations of product and/or design qualities of hybrid products are influenced by country-of-assembly country-of-design, parts-source country, and their interactions.
the country concept is a multidimensional concept and that country-of-origin dimensions should be incorporated into the research designs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
when a product is indicated to be assembled in Mexico, the source of parts is an important factor that influences consumers’ design quality perception.
when a product is indicated as being assembled in a country other than the country-of-design, the parts-source country may affect the consumer's perception of the design quality.
country-of-assembly is a key driver of product quality perception, and that country-of-design is a key driver for design quality perceptions.
